key_insight: TRACER predicted future diagnoses across external health systems, with flagged patients up to eight times more likely to receive a diagnosis within one year at 95% specificity.
clinical_relevance: EHR-based risk prediction could help target disease screening, but detection and false-alert burden vary by disease and health system.
method: Decoder-based foundation model pretrained on longitudinal EHRs from over 4.5 million patients across four health systems.
Evaluated 16 incident diseases at 1-, 2-, and 5-year prediction horizons.
Assessed screening performance at low false-positive rates, including 95% specificity.
evidence_signal: External evaluation included more than 2 million patients from two health systems excluded from model development, where discrimination was retained.
watch_item: Stable overall discrimination did not ensure consistent detection or false-alert burden; local validation is needed before screening implementation.
paper_title: TRACER, a time-to-event EHR foundation model for disease detection across health systems
